articles.title: Same teen suspect wanted in connection with 2 fatal Etobicoke shootings: police
articles.summary: Toronto police say the same teen suspect is linked to two fatal Etobicoke shootings this month.

articles.title: Inquest into death of Mississauga man shot by police in 2020 hears from Peel constable
articles.summary: An inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, who was shot by police in Mississauga, Ont., nearly seven years ago, is hearing Monday from a constable who arrived at the scene after the shooting.

articles.title: 1 man, 2 children dead in Burlington, Ont., house fire, Ontario Fire Marshal says
articles.summary: A man, a 12-year-old child and a one-year-old boy are dead following a house fire in Burlington, Ont., the Ontario Fire Marshal said Monday morning in a news briefing.

articles.title: A Canada Post mail carrier's last day of home delivery in Toronto
articles.summary: Friday was 60-year-old Anita McCulloch’s last day of door-to-door delivery in Rexdale, her beloved northwest Toronto neighbourhood, filled with people she’s grown to care for over the last 2 1/2 years.

articles.summary: Months after construction was supposed to start, safety barriers promised for Toronto’s Leaside Bridge have yet to be installed, and nearby residents are now expressing frustration. articles.title: Milton, Ont., to replace Canada's longest-serving mayor
articles.summary: The town of Milton is set to swear in a new mayor for the first time since 1980. George Minakakis and eight regional and town councillors will take their oaths of office at the council's inaugural meeting Monday night.

articles.title: Thousands tackle 1,776 steps for annual charity CN Tower climb
articles.summary: Thousands of people took on the 1,776 steps to the top of Toronto’s CN Tower for the annual United Way stair climb over the weekend. The event raised nearly $2 million to support community programs across the Greater Toronto Area, including food banks, housing and other essential services. CBC’s Mercedes Gaztambide caught up with some of the climbers.

articles.title: After 6 decades, the future of this Mississauga high school building is uncertain
articles.summary: Hundreds of alumnae and staff gathered on Saturday for a final mass to farewell their former Catholic high school building, which is facing an uncertain future. The Holy Name of Mary College School in Mississauga closed in June due to low enrolment. Its owners, the Felician Sisters of St. Francis, are deciding what to do with the 62 year-old building.

articles.title: 2 workers dead following collision at Pickering construction site: police
articles.summary: Two workers hae died after a collision on a construction site in Pickering on Friday, Durham police say.
